stem:
A stack has been implemented using pseudocode to store a maximum of 100 string items using the global variables in the following table:

[[fig:f1]]

The value of *Top* is incremented each time a data item is added to the stack and decremented each time a data item is removed. If the stack is full, an appropriate error message is output.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
Complete the pseudocode for the procedure to add a data item onto the stack.

```text
PROCEDURE Push ([[blank]])
    IF Top < Max - 1 THEN

        Top ← [[blank]]
        [[blank]] ← NewData
    ELSE

        OUTPUT [[blank]]
    ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE
```

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Write pseudocode to input a new data item and add it to the stack using `Push()`.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain the reasons why a stack is used when a recursive algorithm is executed.

figures.alt: A table listing the identifiers Base, Top, StackArray and Max, with their data types, descriptions and initialisation values.
